meta.title: Tucson Gym Match
meta.subtitle: An honest guide to gyms around 85710: what they really cost, what the spa perks are, and which one fits you.
meta.note: Prices and promotions change often, and many fees vary by club. Everything here was checked on the date above against each gym's own website or the member's own sign-up screens. Confirm the final numbers at the front desk before you sign.

entries.title: Planet Fitness East Broadway: PF Black Card
entries.summary: $24.99 a month, $1 to start and a $49 yearly fee. The membership that unlocks HydroMassage, massage chairs, the red-light booth and tanning, at any Planet Fitness.
body: This is the Planet Fitness membership most people mean when they talk about the massage chairs. At the East Broadway club (7125 E Broadway Blvd, right in 85710) the online offer checked on October 18 and 19, 2026 was $24.99 a month plus tax, a $1 startup fee, a $49 annual fee and no commitment. That offer is marked as expiring November 1.

It is not $29.99 here, at least not yet. Planet Fitness told investors in late 2025 that it planned to raise the Black Card to $29.99 after the 2026 New Year sign-up season. The Tucson clubs checked on October 19, 2026 still list $24.99. If you join now, ask the desk in writing whether your rate is locked if the national price changes; that answer was not published anywhere we could find.

What the Black Card adds over Classic: use of any Planet Fitness club, a free guest every visit, the Black Card Spa (HydroMassage beds, massage chairs, Total Body Enhancement red-light booth, tanning), half-price select drinks, premium app workouts (PF+) and premium partner perks.

Real first-year cost at East Broadway: $1 + (12 × $24.99) + $49 = $349.88 before tax, which works out to about $29.16 a month. That is the number to compare against other gyms, not the $24.99 headline.

details.Recovery perks: HydroMassage, massage chairs, Total Body Enhancement red-light booth, tanning
details.Hours: 24 hours Tue to Thu; Mon 5 AM to midnight; Fri until 10 PM; Sat and Sun 7 AM to 7 PM

entries.title: Planet Fitness East Broadway: Classic
entries.summary: $15 a month, $19 to start and a $49 yearly fee. Full gym floor at one club, but no massage chairs, HydroMassage or red light.
body: The old $10 Planet Fitness is gone. Classic went to $15 a month nationally in 2024, and that is what East Broadway lists: $15 plus tax, a $19 startup fee, a $49 annual fee and no commitment on the current offer.

Classic gets you the gym floor (cardio, machines, the newer plate-loaded strength equipment and free weights), free small-group training, app workouts and Wi-Fi, but only at your home club. The spa area and guest privileges are Black Card only.

Real first-year cost: $19 + (12 × $15) + $49 = $248 before tax, about $20.67 a month. The step up to Black Card costs about $102 more for the year, which is roughly $8.50 a month for the spa, guests and all-club access.

entries.title: Chuze Fitness 22nd & Kolb: Basic
entries.summary: $9.99 a month with a 12-month commitment ($14.99 without), almost nothing to enroll, but a yearly fee of about $60. The cheapest big-box option in 85710.
body: Chuze at 7145 E 22nd St is in 85710 and is the cheapest full-size gym nearby. You are right that there is basically no sign-up fee: the enrollment promotion shown on October 19, 2026 was $0.18.

The fine print matters, though. The $9.99 price requires a 12-month commitment; without a commitment Basic is $14.99. Every Chuze membership has an Annual Membership Fee ($59.99 in the site's fine print, shown as $61.55 on the plan cards, which looks like the fee with tax), charged 45 days after you join and then yearly. Paying by credit card adds $2.99 a month; paying from a bank account avoids it.

Real first-year cost on the 12-month Basic plan, paying by bank draft: $0.18 + (12 × $9.99) + $61.55 = $181.61, about $15.13 a month. Without a commitment: $241.61. Leaving a 12-month plan early can cost $58, and Chuze needs 10 days' written notice before a billing date to cancel.
This location also has a Kids Club (the only Chuze in Tucson with one, per its page), 30-plus weekly classes, a turf area, a Lift Lab and tanning. Basic does not include the classes; Premium does.

entries.title: Chuze Fitness 22nd & Kolb: Premium
entries.summary: $29.99 a month with a 12-month commitment ($34.99 without). Adds classes and is the tier to ask about for HydroMassage and the Recovery Studio.
body: If you like the recovery side of the gym, Chuze 22nd & Kolb has its own: HydroMassage plus a Recovery Studio with massage chairs, red-light therapy, compression boots and a body-composition scanner, according to the club page.

Chuze's pages do not spell out which tier includes the Recovery Studio. Premium is the tier that includes all classes, and it is the usual home for the recovery perks, but treat that as something to confirm at the desk before you pay for it.

Real first-year cost on the 12-month Premium plan by bank draft: $0.18 + (12 × $29.99) + $61.55 = $421.61, about $35.13 a month. That is about $72 a year more than Planet Fitness Black Card, which includes HydroMassage, massage chairs and red light with no commitment. Chuze Premium does add group classes, which Planet Fitness does not have.

entries.title: LA Fitness Wilmot Rd
entries.summary: The pool-and-sauna option about two miles away. Prices are not published online; expect a joining fee and a yearly fee in the $59 to $69 range.
body: LA Fitness at 240 S Wilmot Rd (85711) is the closest LA Fitness to 85710. It has things neither Planet Fitness nor Chuze Basic has: an indoor pool, a sauna, a whirlpool spa, racquetball courts and free group classes. Kids Klub childcare and personal training cost extra.

LA Fitness does not post prices on its club pages; you get them only when you start to join or at the desk. A July 2026 review of LA Fitness official rate pages across the country found monthly dues from $29.99 to $49.99, joining fees from $0 to $99, and an annual fee of $59 to $69. Some clubs also collect the first and last month up front. Tucson numbers were not published, so treat these as ranges, not quotes.

Your instinct to avoid a $49-plus sign-up fee is fair. Ask for the joining fee to be waived; LA Fitness runs $0 enrollment promotions often. Estimated first year at the low end: about $420 ($29.99 × 12 + a $59 annual fee), before any joining fee.
Another LA Fitness is at 9350 E Golf Links Rd (85730), with a pool, sauna, whirlpool and basketball.

details.Monthly: Not published online; national range $29.99 to $49.99
details.First-year cost: Roughly $420 or more (estimate, confirm at desk)
details.Hours: Mon to Thu 5 AM to 11 PM; Fri 5 AM to 10 PM; Sat and Sun 8 AM to 8 PM

entries.title: Ott Family YMCA
entries.summary: $50 a month for an adult, no contract and no separate yearly fee. Two pools, a full gym and classes, right in 85710. May be free with some health plans.
body: The Ott Family YMCA at 401 S Prudence Rd is in 85710. It has a 25-yard lap pool, a warmer recreation pool, a full-size gymnasium, a cycling studio, group exercise, free weights and cardio, plus a Kids Club for members' children.

Pricing is simple: adult (24 and over) $50 a month, dropping to $40 after 12 months in a row; young adults 18 to 23 pay $25; families $80. The Y says its memberships are not contract-based and the joining fee is built into the monthly price. There is no separate annual fee listed. First year for an adult: $600.
Two money-savers worth checking: the Y lists an insurance-based membership at no cost for qualifying health plans, and it offers income-based financial assistance. There is also a free 7-day trial.
There is no massage-chair or red-light spa here; the recovery side is the pool.

details.Monthly: Adult $50 ($40 after 12 months); ages 18 to 23 $25; family $80

entries.title: Clements Fitness Center (City of Tucson)
entries.summary: The city's own gym in Lincoln Regional Park: about $16 a month on an annual pass for city residents, with a weight room, track and courts.
body: The William M. Clements Fitness and Regional Center at 8155 E Poinciana Dr (85730) is run by Tucson Parks and Recreation, a short drive from 85710. It has a weight room, an aerobics room, a walking track, basketball, pickleball and racquetball courts, and locker rooms. The Clements Pool is in the same park.

It uses the city's Universal Pass: $195 a year for an adult city resident ($292.50 for non-residents), $51 a quarter, or $2 a day. Seniors 62 and over pay $133 a year. That is about $16.25 a month for a resident, with no startup or extra yearly fee.

Trade-offs: shorter hours (weekdays 6 AM to 8 PM, Saturday 8 AM to 4 PM, closed Sunday), simpler equipment, and you must take a short certification class before using the weight equipment. The city posted notice in June 2026 that it intends to revise Parks and Recreation fees, so confirm the current rate.

details.Monthly: About $16.25 on the $195 annual pass (city resident)
details.Annual fee: The pass is the fee: $195 resident, $292.50 non-resident
details.Recovery perks: None at the fitness center; pool in the same park
details.Hours: Mon to Fri 6 AM to 8 PM; Sat 8 AM to 4 PM; closed Sun

entries.title: Tucson Strength (independent lifting gym)
entries.summary: A local, old-school strength gym on East Speedway with platforms, racks and strongman gear. Prices are not published; call before you go.
body: If what you want is a serious weight room rather than spa perks, Tucson Strength at 6130 E Speedway Blvd (85712) is the nearby independent option. Directory listings describe powerlifting and Olympic lifting platforms, racks, classic free-weight equipment and coaching.
We could not find official prices or a business website. One gym directory lists about $105 a month, but that figure is unverified. Call or visit before deciding, and ask for a day pass to try it.

entries.title: Other Planet Fitness clubs near you
entries.summary: Swanway Plaza (4722 E Broadway) and Old Spanish Trail (9590 E 22nd St) are both close, and a Black Card works at all of them.
body: Tucson has seven Planet Fitness clubs. The two closest to 85710 besides East Broadway are Swanway Plaza at 4722 E Broadway Blvd (85711) and Old Spanish Trail at 9590 E 22nd St (85748). Both list the same Black Card Spa: HydroMassage, massage chairs, Total Body Enhancement and tanning.

Startup fees and promotions differ by club because most Planet Fitness locations are independently owned franchises. When we checked, Swanway Plaza showed a $39 Classic startup fee and Old Spanish Trail showed a $10 Classic promotion, while all three listed the Black Card at $24.99 with a $49 annual fee. Compare the offer pages before you pick a home club; a Black Card lets you use the others anyway.

entries.title: Is the Black Card $24.99 or $29.99?
entries.summary: Right now in Tucson it is $24.99. Planet Fitness has announced plans to raise it to $29.99 nationally, so you may see that number soon.
body: You are not imagining the $29.99. In November 2025 Planet Fitness told investors it would raise the Black Card from $24.99 to $29.99 after the 2026 peak sign-up season, and in January 2026 its finance chief called $29.99 an incredible value that would still be below the national average gym price.

On October 18 and 19, 2026, the East Broadway, Swanway Plaza and Old Spanish Trail club pages still listed the Black Card at $24.99. Planet Fitness's own October 2026 press kit also says Black Card memberships start at $24.99. Prices are set club by club, so the increase can show up at different times in different places.
The $15 you remember is Classic, which rose from $10 in 2024. Planet Fitness also ran a limited-time $1 down and $10 a month Classic promotion in late summer 2026.

entries.title: Planet Fitness fees and fine print
entries.summary: Yes, there is a yearly fee: $49. There is also a startup fee, a bank-account billing rule, an 8-day cancel deadline and a $58 buyout on commitment plans.
body: Annual fee: $49 a year on both Classic and Black Card at the Tucson clubs we checked. It is billed once a year on your annual fee date. To avoid being charged, your cancellation must reach the club at least 8 days before that date.

Startup fee: varies by club and promotion. At East Broadway it was $1 for Black Card and $19 for Classic. Planet Fitness's own email fine print says memberships may include up to a $49 start-up fee and a 12-month commitment depending on the offer, so make sure the screen you sign on says no commitment.
Billing: many clubs bill from a checking account (EFT) rather than a card. Planet Fitness does not allow partial payments on an overdue balance.

Cancelling: you can cancel by mail to your home club, in person, or online through the member portal. The club must get your notice at least 8 days before your next billing date. If your plan has a minimum term and you end it early, the buyout fee is $58.

details.Startup fee: $1 Black Card, $19 Classic at East Broadway (varies)
details.Cancel deadline: 8 days before the billing date or annual fee date
details.How to cancel: Mail, in person, or online member portal

entries.title: What is in the Black Card Spa (and is there cryo?)
entries.summary: HydroMassage, massage chairs, the Total Body Enhancement red-light booth and tanning. No cryotherapy is listed at the Tucson clubs.
body: HydroMassage: you lie on a padded bed while jets of water move under a waterproof surface. You stay dry and clothed. This is the water massage you described.
Massage chairs: full-body recliner massage chairs, usually on a timer.

Total Body Enhancement: a stand-up booth with red light and a vibration plate, usually a 12-minute session. It is not a sauna; it does not get hot like one. The exact device and light output vary by club and are not published.
Tanning: UV tanning beds or booths. Planet Fitness limits tanning to adults and to no more than once every 24 hours.

Cryotherapy: none of the Tucson club pages list cryotherapy or a cold plunge. Planet Fitness has said it is testing a dry cold plunge and red-light upgrades in select clubs, so ask the East Broadway desk whether anything new is coming.
Rules: phones may not be used for photos, video or calls in the spa area, and amenities can have time and frequency limits.

details.Total Body Enhancement: Red light plus vibration booth, about 12 minutes
details.Tanning: UV beds, adults only, once per 24 hours max
details.Cryotherapy or cold plunge: Not listed at Tucson clubs; being tested elsewhere

entries.title: Will the red light rejuvenate my skin?
entries.summary: Maybe a little, with steady use. Dermatologists say red light may help wrinkles and redness over time, but results are gradual, and gym booths do not publish their dose.
body: A Cleveland Clinic dermatologist said in September 2026 that, when done consistently, research suggests red-light therapy may help with wrinkles and redness, and may help some people with mild hair loss. She also said not to expect overnight results or dramatic changes.

The gym booth is a general-purpose device. Its exact wavelengths and power are not published, and part of what feels good is the vibration plate, which is not light therapy at all. Think of it as a pleasant extra rather than a skin treatment.

Skip it if you burn or blister easily in sunlight, or take medicines that make you sun-sensitive (some antibiotics and blood-pressure drugs). If skin is the main goal, a dermatologist visit is the better investment.

details.Possible benefit: Gradual help with wrinkles and redness with consistent use
details.Limits: Not dramatic; gym booth dose unknown

sources.title: Cleveland Clinic: Can red light therapy improve your skin and hair? (Sept 2026)

entries.title: A word on the tanning beds
entries.summary: Tanning is the one Black Card perk that works against your skin. Dermatologists say there is no safe tanning bed.
body: The American Academy of Dermatology says there is no such thing as a safe tanning bed, booth or sun lamp. It reports that indoor tanning raises the risk of melanoma by 20%, squamous cell carcinoma by 67% and basal cell carcinoma by 29%, and that wrinkles, age spots and loss of firmness show up years earlier in people who tan.
In Tucson you already get plenty of UV outdoors. If skin rejuvenation is a reason you want the Black Card, use the massage and red-light perks and leave the tanning beds alone.

details.Skin aging: Wrinkles and spots appear years earlier

sources.title: American Academy of Dermatology: facts about indoor tanning

entries.title: True first-year cost, side by side
entries.summary: Add the startup fee, twelve months and the yearly fee. On that math, Chuze Basic (12-month plan) and the city pass are cheapest, then Planet Fitness Classic.
body: Monthly prices hide the real cost. Here is each option's first year, using the prices checked October 18 and 19, 2026, before sales tax.

City of Tucson Universal Pass (Clements): $195 for a resident. Chuze Basic, 12-month plan by bank draft: $181.61 (about $15 a month), or $241.61 with no commitment. Planet Fitness Classic: $248. Planet Fitness Black Card: $349.88. Chuze Premium, 12-month plan: $421.61. LA Fitness: roughly $420 or more (estimate). YMCA adult: $600.
Note that Chuze Basic on the 12-month plan edges out the city pass on paper, but the city pass needs no contract and Chuze adds $2.99 a month if you pay by card.
For recovery perks specifically (massage chairs, HydroMassage, red light), Planet Fitness Black Card is the least expensive way to get them, and it has no commitment.

entries.title: So, is the Black Card worth it?
entries.summary: If you will actually use the massage chairs and HydroMassage two or more times a week, yes: it is the cheapest way in 85710 to get them, at about $29 a month all-in.
body: The honest test is use. The Black Card costs about $102 more a year than Classic and about $168 more than Chuze Basic on a 12-month plan. If you use the spa twice a week, that is roughly a dollar or two a visit for a massage-chair or HydroMassage session.

It is also the cheapest recovery package nearby: Chuze 22nd & Kolb has HydroMassage and a Recovery Studio too, but its Premium tier costs about $72 more a year and needs a 12-month commitment for the best price. LA Fitness swaps massage for a pool, sauna and whirlpool at a higher price.

If you mostly want cardio and weights, Chuze Basic or Planet Fitness Classic will do the same job for less. A good plan: use your free Planet Fitness pass and a Chuze guest visit this week, time how often you would really use the spa, and then decide.

details.Worth it if: You use the spa about twice a week or more

entries.title: Questions to ask before you sign anywhere
entries.summary: Get the startup fee, annual fee date, commitment length, cancel rules and price-lock answer in writing.
body: 1. What is the total due today, and what will my first two months of statements show?
2. How much is the annual fee, and on what date is it charged?
3. Is there a commitment? If yes, how long, and what is the early-cancel fee?
4. How do I cancel, and how many days before the billing date must you receive it?
5. Is there a card-processing fee if I do not pay from a bank account?
6. If your national price goes up, is my rate locked?
7. Which perks are included in my tier, and are there time limits on them?
Most gyms will waive or cut a startup fee if you ask, especially near the end of a month.

details.Ask for: Total due today, annual fee date, commitment, cancel notice, card fee, price lock, tier perks

entries.title: Try before you buy
entries.summary: Planet Fitness, LA Fitness and the YMCA all offer free trials, and the city sells a $2 day pass.
body: Planet Fitness gives guest tours and passes at the front desk, and you will get a follow-up email with a link to join. LA Fitness offers a free pass from its club pages. The YMCA has a free 7-day trial. The City of Tucson sells a $2 adult day pass for its recreation centers. A Chuze member can bring you as a guest; Chuze guests get basic gym access only.
Go at the time of day you will really work out, try the exact perks you care about, and check how busy the spa area is.
